data.title: Don't Ignore The Insider Selling In Moog
data.description:
Some Moog Inc. (NYSE:MOG.A) shareholders may be a little concerned to see that the Non-Executive Chairman, John Scannell, recently sold a substantial US$1.0m worth of stock at a price of US$346 per share. However, it's crucial to note that they remain very much invested in the stock and that sale only reduced their holding by 5.3%.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Moog

Notably, that recent sale by Non-Executive Chairman John Scannell was not the only time they sold Moog shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -US$2.1m worth of shares at a price of US$232 per share. That means that even when the share price was below the current price of US$328, an insider wanted to cash in some shares. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. It is worth noting that this sale was only 13% of John Scannell's holding.

John Scannell ditched 15.00k shares over the year. The average price per share was US$283. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. If you click on the chart, you can see all the individual transactions, including the share price, individual, and the date!

Does Moog Boast High Insider Ownership?

I like to look at how many shares insiders own in a company, to help inform my view of how aligned they are with insiders. A high insider ownership often makes company leadership more mindful of shareholder interests. Moog insiders own 1.1% of the company, currently worth about US$114m based on the recent share price. Most shareholders would be happy to see this sort of insider ownership, since it suggests that management incentives are well aligned with other shareholders.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Moog Insiders?

An insider sold stock recently, but they haven't been buying. And there weren't any purchases to give us comfort, over the last year. But it is good to see that Moog is growing earnings. It is good to see high insider ownership, but the insider selling leaves us cautious. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. data.title: There May Be Reason For Hope In Flowers Foods' (NYSE:FLO) Disappointing Earnings
data.description:
Flowers Foods, Inc.'s (NYSE:FLO) earnings announcement last week didn't impress shareholders. While the headline numbers were soft, we believe that investors might be missing some encouraging factors.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

A Closer Look At Flowers Foods' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Flowers Foods has an accrual ratio of -0.11 for the year to October 2026. Therefore, its statutory earnings were quite a lot less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of US$354m, well over the US$30.0m it reported in profit. Flowers Foods shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

Check out our latest analysis for Flowers Foods

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Flowers Foods' profit was reduced by unusual items worth US$190m in the last twelve months, and this helped it produce high cash conversion, as reflected by its unusual items. This is what you'd expect to see where a company has a non-cash charge reducing paper profits. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Flowers Foods took a rather significant hit from unusual items in the year to October 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items made its statutory profit significantly weaker than it would otherwise be.

Our Take On Flowers Foods' Profit Performance

Considering both Flowers Foods' accrual ratio and its unusual items, we think its statutory earnings are unlikely to exaggerate the company's underlying earnings power. After considering all this, we reckon Flowers Foods' statutory profit probably understates its earnings potential! data.title: Is It Smart To Buy Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) Before It Goes Ex-Dividend?
data.description:
Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in three days. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important because any transaction on a stock needs to have been settled before the record date in order to be eligible for a dividend. Therefore, if you purchase Xylem's shares on or after the 24th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 22nd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.43 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed US$1.72 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Xylem has a trailing yield of 1.8% on the current share price of US$95.24. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see Xylem paying out a modest 37% of its earnings. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether Xylem generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. Fortunately, it paid out only 44% of its free cash flow in the past year.

It's positive to see that Xylem's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

Check out our latest analysis for Xylem

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with consistently growing earnings per share generally make the best dividend stocks, as they usually find it easier to grow dividends per share. If business enters a downturn and the dividend is cut, the company could see its value fall precipitously. It's encouraging to see Xylem has grown its earnings rapidly, up 27% a year for the past five years. Earnings per share have been growing very quickly, and the company is paying out a relatively low percentage of its profit and cash flow. Companies with growing earnings and low payout ratios are often the best long-term dividend stocks, as the company can both grow its earnings and increase the percentage of earnings that it pays out, essentially multiplying the dividend.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. Xylem has delivered an average of 11% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past 10 years of dividend payments. Both per-share earnings and dividends have both been growing rapidly in recent times, which is great to see.

The Bottom Line

Is Xylem an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? We love that Xylem is growing earnings per share while simultaneously paying out a low percentage of both its earnings and cash flow. These characteristics suggest the company is reinvesting in growing its business, while the conservative payout ratio also implies a reduced risk of the dividend being cut in the future. It's a promising combination that should mark this company worthy of closer attention.

data.title: What Is Booking Holdings (BKNG) Really Building With Its New AI Travel Push?
data.description:
• Booking Holdings (NasdaqGS:BKNG) created a Booking Partner Division that combines B2B units from Booking.com and Agoda's Rocket Travel.
  • The new division is designed to deliver tailored travel solutions for airline, financial services, and loyalty program partners worldwide.
  • Booking Holdings introduced Vayo, which can assemble and book full itineraries across Booking.com and competing travel platforms using AI tools.
  • KAYAK released 28 AI-driven features that support trip planning, search refinement, and booking assistance across its travel metasearch platform.
  • The Booking Partner Division launch and new AI trip tools change how Booking Holdings works with partners and deserve context beside other risks. We have also flagged 1 warning sign for Booking Holdings.

Plenty of other travel and tech stocks are tied to the same AI booking theme, so it is worth scanning 42 AI small caps.

Booking Holdings operates a global network of travel and restaurant reservation platforms across regions including the US, the Netherlands, and the UK. Expanding its B2B partnerships and AI tools leverages both its consumer reach and its existing relationships with airlines, hotels, and financial services groups.

5 things going right for Booking Holdings that this headline doesn't cover.

How does the Booking Partner Division change Booking Holdings' business model exposure?

Folding Booking.com Strategic Partnerships and Rocket Travel into a single Booking Partner Division concentrates a lot more of Booking Holdings' reach into B2B channels. Banks, airlines and other platforms can plug into white label, API and branded solutions that sit on top of the same 4.7 million properties, 500 airlines and 200 car rental providers already in the system.

Does this Booking Holdings news shift the current Narrative on AI, Connected Trip and efficiency?

The new unit and the AI tools around Vayo and KAYAK line up closely with the existing Narrative. That Narrative leans on the Connected Trip ecosystem, AI driven cost savings and a large direct and loyal customer base. They directly relate to the themes around multi product trips, engineering productivity and supplier partnerships that analysts are already using in their scenarios.

See how these catalysts shape Booking Holdings' path to a $233 fair value.

What should investors watch next to see if Booking's AI and B2B bets are working?

The first potential indicator will be how quickly the Booking Partner Division ramps once it is operational in January 2027, especially new contracts with airlines, banks and travel platforms. On the AI side, early adoption and repeat use of Vayo in private beta, along with uptake of KAYAK's 28 AI features, will show whether travelers and partners continue to use these tools.

data.title: Has Intuit (INTU) Fallen Far Enough After The Mailchimp Sale?
data.description:
Intuit has been hit hard, with the share price around US$310 and the stock down sharply over the past year, so the key question now is whether that lower price is properly supported by the company’s earnings power. With the market also reacting to fresh news about its portfolio and outlook, the current valuation invites a closer look at what investors are really paying for in terms of profit generation.

  • Over the past 5 years, Intuit’s share price has declined 52.8%, which puts the focus squarely on whether the business’s earnings justify even the reduced valuation.
  • The decision to sell Mailchimp for US$3.68b and refocus on AI-driven services may reshape expectations for future profit mix and cash generation, which feeds directly into how its earnings multiple is assessed today.
  • The analysts covering Intuit have run their own numbers. See what analysts think Intuit's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether Intuit’s current share price can be explained by the level and quality of the earnings investors see today.

Does Intuit Look Undervalued on Earnings?

P/E fits Intuit because the company is already profitable and investors are clearly focused on its earnings stream. On this yardstick, Intuit trades on a P/E of 18.1x, which is well below the broader Software sector on 30.5x and also below the peer basket closer to 45.0x. That is a wide gap for a large, established software group whose products are embedded in core workflows for customers.

The Fair Ratio, which reflects what you might expect for Intuit once its growth profile, margins, size and risk are baked in, sits above the current market multiple. Because the stock sold off after the Mailchimp sale and softer Credit Karma outlook, the price now values each dollar of earnings at a discount to what this framework suggests would be typical for the business. For investors, the key question is whether the earnings base that multiple is applied to feels resilient enough to justify closing any part of that gap.
